simple.meaning: בֵּל (Bêl) is a Hebrew word meaning “Bel , the Baal of the Babylonians.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בֵּל (H1078) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 46:1, with occurrences in Isaiah, Jeremiah.

definitions.short: Bel , the Baal of the Babylonians
definitions.full: H1078. Bel בֵּל proper name, masculine a chief Babylonian deity (Babylonian Bêlu = בַּעַל , lord ; Bêl regarded as older form than בַּעַל by Hpt Hebraica. i. 178 ; BAS i. 17) = Merodach (compare מרדך ), tutelary god of Babylon (to be distinguished from older Bêlu , one of ancient Babylonian triad) Jer 50:2 (|| מְרֹדַךְ ) 51:44 ; Isa 46:1 (|| נְבֹו ) — both writers of Babylonian period; — on Bel see COT Gen 11:4 ; Judg 2:11 ; Say Rel. Babylonian 103, 110 Jen Kosmologie 24, 134, 307, 391 .

occurrences.englishText: I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon,
